comments.author: @AustinGlamourPhoto
comments.text: 97 percent OCR means a 3 percent error rate. You try to do engineering math with 3 percent error rate and watch bridges fall apart, LLMs already have a fundamental limitation with randomness built into them (temperature & seeds) which leads to bad generations. Adding a 3 percent error rate on the OCR top of that makes all math, coding and scientific problems completely unsolvable. NOT the path to AGI. Maybe useful for writing fiction or a chat conversation where accuracy doesn't matter but utterly useless for anything where precision matter. Also, Large context windows result in poor generations. Coders run into this all time and have to constantly have clear the content window. This is problem where the larger your prompt gets the more watered down every token is. Eventually you get mush back because Neural net is spread all over the place with too many tokens.  I can not think of single practical use for 1 million token context window anyways.

comments.text: Keep in mind too, that way this OCR model works, it still has text tokens. It reading the text off the images. Still computing in text tokens. There will be a limit to size of the images you are inputting as well the amount of text that you can fit on that resolution of image. At the end of the day, NN compute with tokens. So think of token as unit of compute and the way the models work is they predict the next token.
